props.title: Enchanted
props.initialSlug: A Disney princess finds real love in modern NYC

sections.content: Enchanted (2007) brilliantly deconstructs Disney princess tropes while celebrating them. Amy Adams delivers a star-making performance as Giselle, whose fish-out-of-water journey from animated fairytale to real-world Manhattan creates both hilarious comedy and genuine emotional depth. The film follows in the self-aware footsteps of The Princess Bride (1987), but adds meta-commentary on Disney's own animated classics like Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) and Sleeping Beauty (1959). Director Kevin Lima seamlessly blends traditional 2D animation with live action, paying homage to classic Disney while modernizing the formula. Enchanted|2007|A Disney princess is transported from her animated world to real-life New York City|Disney+ Into the Woods|2014|Subversive take on classic fairy tales with an all-star cast and Sondheim songs|Disney+ Ella Enchanted|2004|Modern twist on Cinderella starring Anne Hathaway as a cursed princess|Prime

The film's musical numbers, particularly "That's How You Know" in Central Park, showcase how Enchanted cleverly translates animated musical conventions into live action spectacle. This technique would later influence Disney's live-action adaptations like Beauty and the Beast (2017) and Aladdin (2019). The songs by Alan Menken and Stephen Schwartz deliberately echo earlier Disney classics while adding contemporary wit, much like Tangled (2010) would do years later.

James Marsden's Prince Edward and Susan Sarandon's Queen Narissa represent perfect parodies of Disney archetypes, while Patrick Dempsey's Robert grounds the story in reality. This balance between fantasy and realism would influence later fairy tale adaptations like Maleficent (2014) and Cinderella (2015), though few achieved Enchanted's perfect tonal balance of sincere romance and gentle satire. The Princess Bride|1987|Classic fantasy romance that playfully subverts fairy tale conventions|Netflix Shrek|2001|Animated fairy tale parody that revolutionized the genre|Peacock Ever After|1998|Realistic retelling of Cinderella starring Drew Barrymore|Hulu SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Fairy Tale Adaptations

Enchanted's success paved the way for more subversive fairy tale adaptations like Mirror Mirror (2012) and Snow White and the Huntsman (2012). The film's ability to both honor and question fairy tale traditions influenced works like Frozen (2013), which similarly challenged princess movie conventions while maintaining the magic audiences love. The upcoming sequel Disenchanted (2022) continues this tradition of examining fairy tale happiness through a modern lens.
